notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5
notes.text: The Ruy Lopez. The bishop pressures the c6 knight that defends e5, and after 3...a6 White keeps the bishop with 4.Ba4.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4
notes.text: The Morphy Defence. Black's main move is 4...Nf6, attacking e4, and White simply answers with 5.O-O.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O
notes.text: White leaves e4 undefended because Re1 will control the open e-file. After 5...Be7, White protects e4 with 6.Re1.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1
notes.text: Now Bxc6 followed by Nxe5 is a real threat. Black usually drives the bishop back with 6...b5, and White retreats to b3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6
notes.text: Black reinforces e5 with ...d6. White plays 8.c3 to prepare d4 and give the b3 bishop a safe home on c2.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O
notes.text: The Closed Ruy Lopez tabiya. White plays 9.h3 to stop ...Bg4 before pushing d4 and routing the knight via Nbd2-f1-g3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O
notes.text: Black castles before playing ...d6, keeping the Marshall Attack in mind. White prevents ...Bg4 and avoids the Marshall with 8.h3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4
notes.text: The Open Variation. Black grabs the e4 pawn, and White strikes at the centre at once with 6.d4.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 b5 Bb3 d5
notes.text: Black locks in the knight on e4. White takes on e5 and supports the centre with c3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4
notes.text: Opening the e-file while Black's king is still in the centre is dangerous. White plays 7.Re1 to pin the knight.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6
notes.text: The Modern Steinitz Defence. White plays 5.c3 first to avoid the Noah's Ark trap and prepare d4 safely.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5 Bb3 Na5
notes.text: Black tries to hunt down the Spanish bishop at once. White calmly castles with 6.O-O and meets ...Nxb3 with axb3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6
notes.text: The Berlin Defence. White keeps the game simple and rich with 4.d3, avoiding the sharp Berlin Endgame.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Bc5
notes.text: Black develops the bishop actively. White prepares d4 and a retreat square for the bishop with 5.c3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 d6
notes.text: Black plays solidly. White prepares d4 with 5.c3 and keeps the Spanish bishop ready to drop back to c2.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5
notes.text: The Classical Defence. White prepares a quick central strike with 4.c3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 c3 Nf6
notes.text: Black attacks e4, and White pushes 5.d4 straight into the centre.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6
notes.text: The Old Steinitz Defence is passive. White takes space in the centre immediately with 4.d4.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5
notes.text: The Schliemann Gambit attacks e4 from the flank. White develops solidly and defends e4 with 4.Nc3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5
notes.text: Black tries to grab the whole centre. White hits back tactically with 6.Nxe5, eyeing Qh5+ and Nxc6.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4
notes.text: The Bird Defence moves the same knight twice. White trades with 4.Nxd4 and castles into a lead in development.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nge7
notes.text: Black avoids doubled pawns with the Cozio Defence. White develops cleanly with 4.Nc3.
